summary: Feed s121_double to SIEM is degraded: 70.6% of traffic is VXLAN-encapsulated and opaque to the tool, and 2.9% of frames exceed the 1518-byte MTU and are dropped by the SIEM NIC.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding VXLAN-encapsulated traffic (1428 of 2023 frames, 70.6%) without stripping the outer header. Likely VXLAN/ERSPAN mirroring from switches is passed straight through to the tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM sees only outer tunnel headers, not inner IP/TCP and application headers, so flow correlation, application identification and detection rules fail on the majority of traffic.

recommended_fix.why: Stripping VXLAN on the packet broker exposes inner L2-L7 headers so the SIEM can parse and correlate flows without needing tunnel-aware decoding.

findings.root_cause: 58 of 2023 frames (2.9%, largest 8108 bytes) exceed the SIEM's 1518-byte MTU, likely jumbo frames plus VXLAN overhead. Broker is not trimming frames to fit the 1 Gbps tool port.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM NIC silently drops oversized frames, creating 2.9% blind spot and incomplete event logging; dropped frames are not analyzed.

recommended_fix.why: SIEM needs_full_payload=false, so slicing/trimming to 1518 bytes on the broker preserves headers for detection while ensuring frames are accepted by the tool port. Also reduces load after tunnel stripping.
